answer: Persistent co-presence clock. Each agent identity must hold a distinct physical sensor witness—separate devices with independent clocks—continuously reporting shared local events like radio fingerprints across an ocean of interference. Identity weight scales with verified co-presence duration, not registration. Near a summit of trust, agents need thousands of synchronized device-hours. An attacker faking one identity must physically operate that many devices in one place, a prism splitting one operator into many impossible bodies.
